findings.artifact_location: FINAL_PROPOSAL.md section 1 C3; sections 3 and 6 validation recommendation
findings.claim: Section 1 generalizes missing-id behavior to warning without any raise for a notebook declaring 4.5 or later.
findings.consequence: A read-only validator using the recommended wrapper fails validity or raises rather than merely warning, so the implementation plan must catch/report invalidity before continuing fallback. This is a material source-condition preservation failure.
findings.independent_result: The warning occurs in _normalize. With repair_duplicate_cell_ids=False, the missing field is left absent; validate then runs iter_validate, whose required-id schema error is raised. isvalid uses that false repair flag and returns False on ValidationError. Default-on repair changes this result by adding the missing id. The statement omits this consequential API/flag condition. Section 3 narrows its statement to _normalize, but does not retract section 1 or specify how the recommended nonmutating validation integrates invalid-id fallback.
findings.proof_kind: independent static call-path and required-field trace; candidate fixtures were not executed

findings.artifact_location: FINAL_PROPOSAL.md section 7 step 3; section 5 scoped engineering lesson
findings.claim: Recovery can mint deterministic content-hash-derived eight-hex ids and describes that as matching the JEP/fix expression family.
findings.consequence: The proposed recovery transform is insufficiently specified to guarantee unique valid notebook ids and is not justified by the cited random generator. This supports the failed source-to-plan screen independently of SQ1.
findings.independent_result: The cited generator is a random UUID subset; JEP distinguishes random generation and requires per-notebook uniqueness. Eight-hex syntax alone does not establish equivalent semantics. Repeated identical-content idless cells can receive the same deterministic content hash; no collision resolution or cell discriminator is specified for minting. The frozen proposal explicitly admits content duplicates in T9, and its own scoped lesson calls for content-independent fields.
findings.proof_kind: source comparison plus deterministic duplicate-content counterexample; no implementation execution
